- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong reversal signals, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply downward bias of 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral/negative), model tends to underperform; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid underestimation.
- Forecast should not exceed 3–5% above recent 7-day average unless sentiment strongly bullish; otherwise, cap at 1–2% above to avoid overreaction.
